the duplicate was made by a machine rather than by a person who was present when the original was executed, and no one can testify to how the copy was made
the original is in the possession of the party who offers the duplicate and was not recently inspected
the duplicate is offered in a case in which the opposing party is an individual rather than an organization

questions.prompt: Ron sues Seth over a written agreement. Ron says the original was destroyed in a flood and offers a copy. Seth says the copy has an altered clause and that he kept the true original, which he declines to produce after receiving notice that its contents would be proved at trial. How should the court proceed on the original-writing issue?
choices: Instruct the jury that the copy is the original as a matter of law because Seth failed to produce the document upon request
Allow other evidence of the contents under Rule 1004(c), since Seth had control of the original and was notified, and let the jury decide which writing is accurate under Rule 1008
Exclude all evidence of the agreement's contents because the original is unavailable and no exception applies to a party's refusal
Require Ron to prove the contents solely by Seth's testimony, since Seth is the only person with the original in his possession

questions.prompt: In a fraud trial, the prosecution has 15,000 pages of bank records, admissible and made available to the defense, and offers an accountant's chart totaling the transfers. choices: Neither chart is permitted because the originals of voluminous records must always be read aloud in court

questions.prompt: Under Rule 606(b), during an inquiry into the validity of a verdict, a juror may testify about:
choices: whether the juror's own vote was influenced by a statement made in deliberations
whether a fellow juror misunderstood the judge's instructions on the burden of proof
whether other jurors failed to give fair consideration to the evidence during deliberations
whether extraneous prejudicial information was improperly brought to the jury's attention

questions.prompt: During a trial, counsel hands a witness a notebook she kept at the scene, and she says it refreshed her memory. She then testifies from memory. What rights does the opposing party have under Rule 612?
choices: To have the notebook read to the jury as an exhibit by the proponent regardless of whether it is otherwise admissible
To have the notebook sealed, since a writing used to refresh memory is protected as work product in every circumstance
To have the notebook produced, inspect it, cross-examine her on it and introduce relevant portions, if she used it while testifying
To exclude her testimony entirely, because a witness may not use any writing to refresh her recollection at the time of trial

questions.prompt: A civil defendant calls a witness who works for the plaintiff's competitor and is clearly hostile to the defendant. The defendant wants to ask leading questions on direct. Under Rule 611(c)?
choices: The court may allow leading questions only if the witness is a child under the age of ten
The court may allow leading questions because the witness is hostile or identified with an adverse party
The court may never allow leading questions on direct examination under any circumstances
The court must allow leading questions because the witness was called by the defendant

questions.prompt: After a criminal verdict, a juror submits an affidavit saying that during deliberations the foreperson read aloud a newspaper article about the defendant that was not in evidence, and another juror says she voted guilty mainly because she was worn down by the others. Both statements, because a juror may testify about every event during deliberations if the verdict is challenged in good faith
Neither statement, because Rule 606(b) bars all testimony of jurors about deliberations in every circumstance without exception
Only the juror's account of being worn down, because mental processes are an exception to the rule for coercion claims

questions.prompt: After a criminal trial, a juror reports that another juror said during deliberations that the defendant was guilty because he is of a particular ethnicity, expressing animus in clear terms. The defense moves for a new trial. What is the best analysis?

The evidence is admissible only if the juror made the statement outside the jury room and before the deliberations began
The evidence is admissible only if the biased juror is willing to testify voluntarily about her own state of mind
Under Pena-Rodriguez v. Colorado, the no-impeachment rule yields when a juror made a clear statement showing reliance on racial animus to convict, so the court may consider the evidence

questions.prompt: Under Rule 609(a)(2), a conviction must be admitted to impeach a witness if:
choices: the court can readily determine that establishing the elements required proving, or the witness admitting, a dishonest act or false statement
the crime was a felony and the witness is a defendant whose testimony is central to the defense
the conviction is less than five years old and the crime was punishable by more than a month in jail
the witness lied about the conviction in an earlier deposition and the opposing party offers the deposition

questions.prompt: On cross-examination, counsel asks a witness whether she once lied on a loan application, which is an uncharged act. The witness denies it. May counsel then prove the lie with a bank employee's testimony under Rule 608(b)?
choices: No, because Rule 608(b) allows no inquiry about specific acts that did not result in a criminal conviction
No, because extrinsic evidence of specific instances is not admissible to prove untruthful character under Rule 608(b)
Yes, because any act of dishonesty can be proved by outside witnesses whenever the witness denies it on cross
Yes, but only if the bank employee is called by the court rather than by the opposing party

questions.prompt: At a civil trial, a witness for the defendant says he saw the plaintiff run the red light. The plaintiff has evidence that the witness is the defendant's brother-in-law and stands to inherit if the defendant wins the suit. May the plaintiff offer this?
choices: No, because the rule on specific instances of conduct forbids any reference to financial interest
Yes, but only if the witness first admits the relationship during preliminary questions by the judge
Yes, because bias and interest are never collateral and may be shown by extrinsic evidence
No, because only a party's own relatives may be impeached by questions about family ties

questions.prompt: Mara is on trial for assault and testifies in her own defense. The prosecutor seeks to impeach her with an eight-year-old felony conviction for armed robbery, not involving dishonesty. Mara objects. Which approach does Rule 609 require?

Exclude automatically, because convictions for violent crimes never bear on a witness's truthfulness
Admit automatically under Rule 609(a)(2) because armed robbery is a crime of dishonesty by its nature
Balance under Rule 609(a)(1)(B): admit only if the probative value of the conviction outweighs its prejudicial effect to Mara

questions.prompt: Tomas, a criminal defendant, has a prior felony conviction. The court rules in limine that it will admit it if he testifies. Tomas decides not to testify and is convicted. On appeal he argues that the ruling was error. Under Luce v. United States, what is the likely result?

The claim succeeds only if Tomas proves that his testimony would have changed the verdict
The claim is reviewable only if the prosecutor agrees that the ruling affected the defendant's decision

questions.prompt: Which is a proper lay opinion under Rule 701?
choices: A witness's testimony that a bullet wound is consistent with a particular weapon caliber, based on forensic training
A bystander's testimony that the driver seemed drunk based on how he walked and spoke
A witness's opinion that a company's accounting method violates professional standards after only a brief training course
A witness's statement that a pharmaceutical dose is safe, based on scientific literature he has reviewed

questions.prompt: Under Rule 703, if facts or data on which an expert relies would be inadmissible, the proponent may disclose them to the jury only if:

the opposing party stipulates to their reliability before the expert begins to testify
they were obtained by a government agency through a legally authorized investigation
the expert personally generated the facts or data in the course of preparing the opinion

questions.prompt: In a criminal prosecution in which the defendant pleads insanity, a psychiatrist testifies. Under Rule 704(b), which testimony is prohibited?

That the defendant's medical records document treatment for the disorder before the offense
That the defendant did not have the mental state that constitutes an element of the crime or a defense

questions.prompt: At a drug-distribution trial, the prosecutor calls the arresting officer, who did not qualify as an expert, to testify that, from his years of narcotics experience, the numbers and abbreviations in the defendant's notebook are code for amounts and prices. Overrule; any witness with personal experience in a field may give lay opinion about the meaning of documents

a jury, not the judge, must decide whether an expert's methodology is sufficiently reliable to be considered
Rule 702 superseded the Frye general-acceptance test in federal courts and requires the judge to assess reliability and relevance
general acceptance in the scientific community is the sole requirement for admitting expert evidence in federal court

Whether the Frye test continues to apply in federal civil cases involving claims of manufacturing defects
Whether experts may state legal conclusions about whether a product was defective under state law
Whether the Daubert gatekeeping obligation applies to expert testimony based on technical or other specialized knowledge, not only scientific knowledge

De novo review, because reliability of science is a pure question of law
Clear error review, because the trial court makes findings of fact on every Daubert factor
Review only when the jury, rather than the judge, made the reliability determination

Animal studies are categorically inadmissible in federal court because they were not conducted on human subjects
The expert must be excluded because an expert may never rely on any evidence that is not independently admissible

Whether the technique has gained general acceptance in the relevant scientific community
Whether the technique has a known or potential error rate and controlling standards

the law of the forum state only if the parties have signed a choice-of-law agreement

both spouses together, so that both must consent before testimony is allowed

licensed psychotherapists, including licensed clinical social workers, during diagnosis or treatment
